description: Pretrained weights for BanditRouter v2 with Feature Linearization. Maps model archetypes to initial theta weights providing 'Initial Intuition' while maintaining 'High Plasticity' (A = λI).

feature_structure.description: Feature vector structure with linearized signals (total 54 dims with PCA)
dims: - Original (7): code_heavy, requires_json, input_length_log, list_density, instruction_density, flesch, toxicity
- Linearized (8): has_code_block, code_block_log, has_latex, latex_log, has_question, question_log, length_bin, length_log

reasoning_model.description: High-capability models (HLE > 0.15): claude-opus-4.5, gpt-5, o3, grok-4, sonnet-4.5, oss-120b, etc.
reasoning_model.rationale: Step functions (has_latex=2.0) provide massive boost when hardness indicators present. Continuous slopes (latex_density_log=0.5) add incremental difficulty. Negative bias requires proof of complexity.

turbo_model.description: Fast/cheap models (HLE < 0.10): gpt-4o, haiku-4.5, llama-3.1-70b, ministral-8b, gemma-3, etc.
turbo_model.rationale: Negative step functions (has_latex=-2.0) strongly penalize ANY hardness. Negative slopes prevent selection as difficulty grows. Positive bias wins by default for simple prompts.

usage_notes: Feature Linearization (v2.0): Binary features capture step functions, log features capture slopes.
The loader in _load_zero_shot_priors maps each model to an archetype based on HLE score:
Key insight: 'Having 50 LaTeX equations isn't 50x harder than having 1' - that's what log scaling captures.
The bandit learns quickly from user feedback, so these are just starting points.
